actions.justification: Mandatory first step - patient has tachycardia (HR 105), tachypnea (RR 22), and hypoxemia (SpO2 93%) requiring formal vital signs assessment to establish baseline and risk stratification.
Mandatory action - Wells score assessment required for PE risk stratification per ESC PE guidelines, even with confirmed CTPA, to guide management pathway.
Mandatory diagnostic test per PE guidelines. D-dimer ordered as part of initial workup to support risk stratification and management decisions.
Patient has SpO2 of 93% with acute dyspnea from confirmed PE. Supplemental oxygen is indicated to correct hypoxemia and reduce hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction per ESC PE guidelines.

12-lead ECG is indicated to assess for right heart strain patterns (S1Q3T3, new RBBB, sinus tachycardia) which help risk-stratify PE severity and evaluate for alternative diagnoses. Also aligns with AHA chest pain guideline for acute chest pain workup.

PE is confirmed on CTPA. ESC guidelines state anticoagulation should not be delayed in confirmed PE. Patient is hemodynamically stable (BP 130/82, MAP 98) without shock, so therapeutic anticoagulation should be initiated promptly.

Echocardiogram is indicated to assess right ventricular function and size, which determines PE severity stratification (massive vs submassive). With HR 105 and SpO2 93%, RV dysfunction would indicate high-risk PE requiring escalated therapy. Critical for risk stratification per ESC PE guidelines.

Pulmonology consultation is appropriate given confirmed PE in a morbidly obese patient (BMI 58) with hypoxemia (SpO2 93%), tachycardia, and tachypnea. Complex management decisions including antibiotic dosing adjustments for obesity and potential escalation may be needed.

Chest X-ray is useful to evaluate for alternative or concurrent diagnoses (pneumonia, pleural effusion, pneumothorax) and to assess baseline cardiopulmonary status in this dyspneic patient with confirmed PE.

Lower extremity venous Doppler ultrasound is indicated in confirmed PE to assess for concurrent DVT, which informs anticoagulation management and risk stratification per ESC PE guidelines. This has not yet been performed.

Echocardiogram is critical for risk stratification in confirmed PE to assess right ventricular strain and function. Morbid obesity (BMI 58) increases RV afterload risk. RV dysfunction would escalate to intermediate-high or high-risk PE classification and may influence treatment escalation decisions.

Serial ECG to assess for signs of RV strain (S1Q3T3 pattern, new RBBB, sinus tachycardia) in this confirmed PE patient with tachycardia and hypoxia, aiding in risk stratification per ESC PE guidelines.
SpO2 93% warrants ABG to quantify hypoxemia severity, assess A-a gradient, and evaluate for respiratory acidosis or compensatory changes in this PE patient.
BNP is a key biomarker for right ventricular strain and PE risk stratification (ESC PE guidelines); elevated BNP indicates higher mortality risk and may influence treatment intensity decisions.
Basic metabolic panel provides baseline renal function (important for anticoagulation dosing, especially in morbidly obese patient) and electrolytes to guide management.

CBC is warranted to assess for baseline hemoglobin/hematocrit (important before anticoagulation decisions in a morbidly obese patient), platelet count, and white cell count. Not yet completed and relevant to ongoing PE management.
Coagulation studies (PT/INR, aPTT) are essential to guide anticoagulation dosing and monitoring in confirmed PE, especially important in morbid obesity where dosing adjustments may be needed.

Serum lactate helps assess for tissue hypoperfusion/shock physiology. With SpO2 93% and HR 105, occult hemodynamic compromise must be evaluated to stratify PE severity and guide escalation decisions (e.g., thrombolysis vs anticoagulation alone).

Troponin is a key risk stratification biomarker in confirmed PE. Elevated troponin indicates RV myocardial injury and upgrades the patient to intermediate-high or high risk, guiding decisions on escalation of therapy. This has not yet been ordered and is critical for prognostication in this hemodynamically stable but tachycardic, hypoxic patient.

Patient has confirmed PE on CTPA and is hemodynamically stable (no hypotension/shock). ESC guidelines recommend prompt anticoagulation without delay. LMWH (e.g., enoxaparin weight-adjusted) is first-line for intermediate-risk PE. Although 'give_anticoagulation' is listed as already done, 'give_lmwh' is a distinct available action — if anticoagulation has been initiated, this confirms/specifies the agent. If not yet concretely administered, LMWH should be given now given BMI 58 (morbid obesity requires weight-based dosing).

Patient has confirmed PE with SpO2 93%, HR 105, and is hemodynamically stable. Anticoagulation with IV unfractionated heparin is indicated per ESC PE guidelines. Given BMI 58 (morbid obesity), UFH via weight-based IV dosing is preferred over LMWH for reliable dosing and monitoring in this patient. Prior give_anticoagulation/give_lmwh entries may reflect initial orders, but IV heparin infusion ensures therapeutic anticoagulation in this high-BMI patient.

Given morbid obesity (BMI 58) and confirmed PE with borderline hypoxia and tachycardia, early consultation with interventional radiology is appropriate to evaluate catheter-directed therapy as an option if the patient deteriorates or is found to have high-risk/intermediate-high-risk PE on risk stratification.

Patient with confirmed PE has HR 105 and SpO2 93% with hemodynamic stability. Cautious IV fluid administration may support RV preload. This is the most appropriate available action given anticoagulation is already initiated, the patient is hemodynamically stable (ruling out thrombolysis and vasopressors), and repeat CT-PA is not indicated.

Patient has confirmed PE with persistent tachycardia (HR 105), hypoxia (SpO2 93%), and elevated RR (22), suggesting submassive or high-risk PE with signs of right heart strain. With anticoagulation already initiated, thrombolysis should be considered given hemodynamic compromise markers and high clot burden risk in this morbidly obese, immobilized patient. ESC PE guidelines support thrombolytic therapy for high-risk PE or deteriorating intermediate-high risk PE.
